title: Synchronize PRD decision anchors and dependency ownership across Eng/Design/Legal
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Create a durable, lightweight process that attaches explicit decision anchors to PRD sections (requirements, scope changes, acceptance criteria) and assigns clear owners for any cross-team dependency (Eng/Design/Legal). This ticket produces a template, a small automation for owner notifications, and a one-pager for reviewers to speed sign-off windows for medium-risk platform changes. Scope: schema for PRD decision anchors, owner matrix, Slack/Calendar notification pattern, sample completed PRD, and a short runbook for contingency when an owner is unavailable. Out of scope: implementing org-wide automation (this is a pilot for infra/runtime and console teams).
acceptance_criteria: Decision anchor schema defined and added to PRD template: decision_id, rationale, options considered, decision_owner, review_deadline, rollback_plan
Owner matrix for typical dependency types published (API change, privacy/data-handling, UX flow, infra rollout) and reviewed by Eng/Design/Legal leads
Automation: a lightweight Zap/Flow that pings the decision_owner and the ’eng/pm/design/legal-review’ Slack channel when a decision_anchor is added and the review_deadline is within 72 hours
Sample PRD (runtime batching change) annotated with decision anchors and signed off by stakeholders in the pilot group
Runbook for when a decision_owner is unavailable (delegate list + escalation path) documented and approved
No open critical blockers from Legal on the pilot PRD; any open issues are captured as follow-up tickets with owners and deadlines
progress_updates: 2025-11-12: Initial draft created during PRD working session. Captured common friction points: unclear ownership on privacy reviews, last-minute UX asks, and vague rollout criteria.

2025-11-18: Workshop with Eng/Design/Legal leads (Sofia Martinez, Ravi Singh, Maya Chen). Agreed to decision anchor schema; Legal requested an explicit data-residency field for all anchors that touch telemetry.

2025-11-24: Prototype PRD template updated in Confluence; added 'decision_owner' and 'escalation_contact' fields. Circulated for review. Noted potential friction with existing Jira/Linear flows — follow-up with Platform Integrations engineers required.

2025-11-28: Built proof-of-concept notification Flow to Slack; sends message and creates a draft Linear sub-issue when review_deadline < 72h. Flow currently stores metadata in a shared Google Sheet for the pilot.

2025-12-02: Pilot PRD (runtime-batching) annotated and reviewed by pilot stakeholders; Legal sign-off pending clarification on telemetry retention wording. Created follow-up PM-143900 to resolve retention language with Legal.
2025-12-02: Eng lead (Ravi Singh) flagged need for explicit testing acceptance criteria tied to latency SLOs; added to acceptance checklist and created dependency ENG-29421 for test harness work.
decision_log: 2025-11-18: Adopted minimal decision_anchor schema (decision_id, description, options considered, owner, deadline, rollback_plan). Rationale: small cognitive overhead encourages adoption.

2025-11-18: Legal requested telemetry/data-residency metadata for any anchor that touches runtime telemetry or customer data. Decision: add optional 'data_residency' and 'legal_notes' fields to schema.

2025-11-24: Agreed that the PRD template will include a pre-review checklist that must be completed before wide circulation: stakeholders listed, review_deadline set, and at least one dependency identified with owner. Rationale: reduces last-minute async clarifications.
2025-12-02: For pilot, notification flow will create a Linear sub-issue instead of requiring reviewers to subscribe to Confluence. Rationale: linear tasks drive actionability.
2025-12-02: Contingency escalation path accepted: primary owner -> designated delegate -> Eng/PM/Design on-call lead. Rationale: keeps decision latency bounded during holiday/off hours.
blockers: Legal wording on telemetry retention not finalized (blocking Legal sign-off for pilot PRD)
Platform integrations engineer bandwidth to replace Google Sheet proof-of-concept with internal metadata store (ETA dependent on ENG-30011)
notes_for_reviews: Design: please validate that the owner matrix covers emergent UX flows that require legal review (esp. structured output changes).
Legal: confirm if the 'data_residency' field is sufficient for fast triage, or if Legal prefers a separate data assessment form.
Engineering: review the prototype notification flow and suggest safe rate limits for automated Linear sub-issues to avoid noise.
